name: Household Robot Vacuum
definition: An autonomous dry-cleaning robot designed for household floors that uses onboard sensing, navigation, drive, brushes, an airflow path, a dust bin, a battery and a charging dock; combination models are included only within their documented vacuuming function.
includedScope: Vacuum-and-mop combination robots when evaluating their documented dry pickup, navigation and dock system
excludedScope: Commercial cleaning robots and ride-on autonomous floor scrubbers
Pool, window, lawn and mopping-only robots
Unverified claims that a single suction, navigation or obstacle value proves whole-home performance
primaryApplications: Scheduled household hard-floor and carpet pickup
Between-clean maintenance in pet and mixed-floor homes
Autonomous room coverage with return-to-charge and optional dock automation
headline: Household robot vacuum navigation, pickup, docks, data and buyer checks
description: This profile separates navigation and obstacle handling from dry pickup, battery, dock automation, consumables and connected-data controls so buyers can test the complete robot-home system.
metaDescription: Household robot vacuum guide covering navigation, dry pickup, brushes, batteries, docks, models, standards, data and buyer checks.
disclaimer: This independent category reference is not operating, cybersecurity, privacy, battery, surface-care or safety advice. Confirm the exact regional model, manual, floor and threshold limits, dock utilities, app and data policy, consumables and approved surfaces before procurement or use.

keyFacts.label: Category boundary
keyFacts.value: Autonomous dry-cleaning robot for household floors
keyFacts.evidence: IEC/ASTM 62885-7 addresses dry-cleaning robots and official pages identify autonomous household vacuuming functions.
keyFacts.scope: Combination models are assessed only within documented dry-cleaning functions.

keyFacts.label: System boundary
keyFacts.value: Robot, floor plan, thresholds, dock, app and consumables operate together
keyFacts.evidence: Official models combine sensing, drive, pickup, charging, dock and connected controls in different configurations.
keyFacts.scope: Exact regional product and actual home.

keyFacts.label: Performance method
keyFacts.value: IEC/ASTM 62885-7:2020 provides household dry-cleaning robot performance methods
keyFacts.evidence: IEC publishes the standard scope for covered dry-cleaning robots.
keyFacts.scope: Matched laboratory methods; not every catalogue claim cites the standard.

keyFacts.label: Buyer verification
keyFacts.value: Test navigation, pickup, recovery, dock work, consumables and data controls
keyFacts.evidence: No reviewed single specification covers the whole operating result.
keyFacts.scope: Representative floor plan and exact firmware or app version.

systemFlow.name: Perception and mapping
systemFlow.componentFamily: Distance, obstacle, cliff, contact and optional camera sensors
systemFlow.role: Detects boundaries and inputs for navigation or avoidance.
systemFlow.evidence: Official pages describe distinct sensor and navigation systems.
systemFlow.scope: Detection claims are object, lighting and environment specific.

systemFlow.name: Planning and drive
systemFlow.componentFamily: Controller, mapping software, wheels and suspension
systemFlow.role: Plans motion, crosses approved transitions and recovers from interruptions.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers publish product-specific navigation and threshold claims.

systemFlow.name: Dry pickup
systemFlow.componentFamily: Side brush, main brush, suction fan, bin and filter
systemFlow.role: Moves dry debris from the floor into onboard collection.
systemFlow.evidence: Official products identify brush, suction and bin systems.

systemFlow.name: Energy and docking
systemFlow.componentFamily: Battery, charge contacts and base station
systemFlow.role: Supports autonomous return, charging and optional dust or mop-service functions.
systemFlow.evidence: Reviewed systems range from simple charge bases to multi-function docks.

systemFlow.name: Connected control
systemFlow.componentFamily: App, network, account, updates and data services
systemFlow.role: Provides scheduling, mapping, settings and support functions where offered.
systemFlow.evidence: Official pages and manuals describe model-specific connected features.
systemFlow.scope: Region, app version, account and network dependencies.

variants.name: Vacuum-only robot with charge base
variants.operatorRelationship: User empties the onboard bin and services brushes and filters
variants.spaceConstraints: Charge-base clearance and accessible floor transitions
variants.limitations: Simple docking does not remove daily bin or brush maintenance.
variants.evidence: iRobot publishes a household vacuuming robot with charging base.

variants.name: Vacuum-and-mop robot with multifunction dock
variants.taskScale: Scheduled mixed dry and wet floor-care routines
variants.operatorRelationship: User services dust, water, cleaning media and dock surfaces
variants.spaceConstraints: Larger dock, power, ventilation and possible water handling
variants.limitations: Wet functions do not prove dry pickup and increase maintenance paths.
variants.evidence: Roborock, ECOVACS, Dreame, Narwal and Eufy publish multifunction systems.

variants.name: Low-profile or adaptive-navigation robot
variants.taskScale: Homes with low furniture, thresholds or complex obstacles
variants.operatorRelationship: User maps risk zones and maintains sensors
variants.spaceConstraints: Furniture clearance, thresholds, cables and reflective surfaces
variants.limitations: Maximum obstacle or height claims use model-specific conditions.
variants.evidence: Roborock and Dreame publish adaptive-height or threshold features.

performanceMetrics.name: Dry debris pickup
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Removal of specified material from stated hard-floor or carpet tests
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Debris, surface, brush, passes, bin state and method matter
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not infer pickup from maximum suction pressure alone.
performanceMetrics.evidence: IEC/ASTM defines performance methods for dry-cleaning robots.

performanceMetrics.name: Coverage and navigation
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Ability to traverse and clean accessible areas without excessive omission or repetition
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Floor plan, lighting, obstacles, thresholds, firmware and starting state matter
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: A sensor label does not prove whole-home coverage.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources publish different navigation architectures.

performanceMetrics.name: Obstacle and threshold handling
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Ability to detect, avoid or cross specific objects and transitions
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Object type, geometry, color, lighting and approach angle affect results
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Maximum threshold height is not universal obstacle clearance.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers qualify object and threshold claims by conditions.

performanceMetrics.name: Runtime and area claim
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Mode, floor, obstacles, battery state and dock behavior change results
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Minutes or square metres alone do not establish completed coverage.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official pages state product-specific batteries or runtime claims.

performanceMetrics.name: Dock service interval
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Frequency of dust, water, bag, tray and cleaning-media intervention
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Soil load, home size, pets and selected functions dominate
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Maximum hands-free-day claims are not fixed service intervals.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Multifunction dock pages publish model-specific storage and automation claims.

applicationFit.assessment: Run the exact robot through a representative furnished route and separately score dry pickup, transitions and recovery.

applicationFit.evidence: Official products target household mixed-floor routes with different systems.

applicationFit.assessment: Use representative hair, cables, toys and low-contrast objects in a controlled trial.

applicationFit.limitations: No obstacle system guarantees avoidance of every hazard or pet waste.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Create no-go zones and record contacts, entanglement and maintenance time.
applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturers publish hair and obstacle-management features with limitations.

applicationFit.assessment: Measure all human work, including pre-tidying, bin or bag, water, tray, brush, sensor and recovery tasks.

applicationFit.limitations: Maximum interval claims depend on soil load and use.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Run a multi-week trial and log every intervention and consumable.
applicationFit.evidence: Official multifunction docks automate different subsets of work.

procurementDecisions.intendedTask: Automate dry pickup across a real home
procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Coverage, pickup and intervention rate together
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Ranking by maximum suction or sensor count
procurementDecisions.assessment: Require a furnished-route trial with measured dry debris and logged interventions.
procurementDecisions.basis: No single component specification establishes whole-home performance.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Results remain floor-plan and firmware dependent.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Record missed areas, pickup, contacts, stalls, recharge and manual recovery.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm threshold, stair, rug and furniture clearances.
procurementDecisions.evidence: IEC provides performance methods while official products use different navigation systems.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Total dock and robot intervention workload
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating maximum hands-free days as a guaranteed interval
procurementDecisions.assessment: Log every task over multiple representative weeks.
procurementDecisions.basis: Dust, water, brushes, sensors and dock surfaces have separate service needs.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Soil and pet load vary widely.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Price bags, filters, brushes, cleaning media and dock parts for three years.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify dock power, clearance, drainage or refill needs.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official multifunction docks automate different work packages.

procurementDecisions.intendedTask: Use connected maps and remote controls
procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Account, network, data, update and offline behavior
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Assuming app convenience carries no lifecycle dependency
procurementDecisions.assessment: Include privacy and software support in procurement acceptance.
procurementDecisions.basis: Connected features depend on services beyond the robot hardware.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Policies and features can change after verification.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Review current privacy notice, permissions, deletion, support term and outage behavior.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Segment home network where appropriate and document reset before disposal.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official products offer app-connected mapping or scheduling.
procurementDecisions.scope: Region, account, app and firmware version.

engineeringChecks.reason: The robot can become stranded, fall, collide or miss inaccessible areas.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Measure the floor plan and perform supervised boundary tests before scheduling.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturer navigation and obstacle claims are geometry dependent.

engineeringChecks.reason: Hair, string, dust and filter loading change pickup and can stop moving parts.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Inspect after representative cycles and set written cleaning and replacement intervals.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official products use model-specific brush, bin and filter systems.

engineeringChecks.reason: Charge contacts, pack condition and dock placement affect autonomous completion.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Verify dock clearance, circuit, battery code and replacement path.
engineeringChecks.evidence: IEC includes automatic battery-operated cleaners and docking requirements; manufacturers define exact docks.

engineeringChecks.reason: Maps, cameras, accounts, cloud services and updates create privacy and support dependencies.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Review current policies and test local, offline, reset and account-deletion behavior.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Reviewed products offer connected control and some include camera-based perception.

standards.name: IEC/ASTM 62885-7:2020
standards.applicability: Performance measurement methods for covered household dry-cleaning robots.
standards.scope: Dry-cleaning performance; combination wet functions require separate evidence.

standards.applicability: Safety requirements for covered household vacuum cleaners, including automatic battery-operated cleaners and docking-related requirements.
standards.evidence: IEC publishes the edition scope and changes.
standards.scope: Confirm national adoption and exact conformity.
